title: Git security vulnerabilities announced
author: Elijah Newren
description: Git is releasing updates addressing six security vulnerabilities affecting clones, reference handling, merges, binary patches, and imports. Here is what users need to know. The post Git security vulnerabilities announced appeared first on The GitHub Blog .
summary: Editor’s note (November 17, 2026): This post has been updated with additional CVE information and updated guidance for GitHub Enterprise Server users . Please see the release information below for the versions that include the fixes.
takeaways: We recommend updating to Git 2.56.1 or the patched release for your maintenance series, and updating any applications that bundle Git.

The release also validates other reference names and symbolic-reference targets received through protocol v2. [ Advisory ] CVE-2026-114467: Stack corruption when removing signatures When stripping GPG signatures from a message, Git assumed there would be at most two signatures.

Git now also checks the declared uncompressed size before processing a binary patch. [ Advisory ] CVE-2026-105437: Heap corruption during large merges Git’s merge machinery calculates how much memory it needs for a merge result before writing the output.
